extracted.intended_audience: microbiologists, taxonomists, systematists, and other biological scientists working with scientific names and nomenclature codes
extracted.subtask_description: An annotated overview and bibliographic guide to the major international Codes of Nomenclature (prokaryotes, plants, animals, viruses, cultivated plants, phytosociology) and related reference lists and resources used to validly publish, conserve, reject, and find scientific names.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes (ICNP)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early drafts of the International Bacteriological Code of Nomenclature were published in 1947 and reprinted in the Journal of Bacteriology in 1948. The first edition of the code approved by the Judicial Commission was published as an annotated book in 1958 as the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria and Viruses. The 1966 revision was published in article form only ... Subsequent editions were published as books in 1975 (1976 Revision) and 1992 (1990 Revision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formerly known under several names (International Code of Nomenclature of Procaryotes, International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria (ICNB), Prokaryotic Code, Bacteriological Code). Citations and edition history are provided (1947, 1948, 1958, 1966, 1975, 1992).

rubrics_metrics.name: International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants (ICN)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first international rules governing botanical nomenclature were established in 1867 at the Fourth International Botanical Congress in Paris. Various conflicting and reconciled codes and revisions (Vienna Rules 1906, American Code 1907, Cambridge Rules 1935) and many subsequent named 'Codes' (Stockholm, Paris, Montreal, Edinburgh, Seattle, Leningrad, Sydney, Berlin, Tokyo, Saint Louis, Vienna, Melbourne etc.) are listed with dates and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a historical chain of adopted botanical codes and their editions (with publication citations) that define the rules used for botanical nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants (ICNCP)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first edition of the ICNCP was formally proposed in 1952, with the first edition published in 1953 and later revisions following; the Code governs nomenclature for cultivated plants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists successive editions and major references (1953 origin, 1958/1961/1969/1980/1995/2005/2009 editions) and notes the informal name 'Cultivated Plant Code'.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN Code)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several 19th-century rule sets preceded internationally accepted rules; the first International Rules on Zoological Nomenclature were published in 1905 and amended across the 20th century. A major revision published as the first edition of the ICZN Code appeared in 1961, with later editions (1964 second edition, 1985 third edition, 1999 fourth edition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides edition history and references; identifies the Code as the formal rules for zoological nomenclature and lists book lengths and publishers for major editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Code of Nomenclature of Viruses / International Code of Virus Classification and Nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: The nomenclature of viruses was covered under the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria and Viruses until 1966, when an independent code was proposed for viruses. Ratified changes to the International Code of Nomenclature of Viruses will be published in Virology Division News in Archives of Virology, and in subsequent ICTV Reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises that ratified changes and actions on proposals to change the code are documented in ICTV Minutes and Reports; references to historical reports and editions are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: BioCode (Draft BioCode)
rubrics_metrics.description: An initiative (meeting in March 1994) to investigate harmonizing the five major Codes of Nomenclature; the project failed to receive support for implementation by 2000. A revised draft of the BioCode was published in 2011 and continues to seek support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists key publications and commentary (Draft BioCode 2011, related special issues and articles) and frames the BioCode as a prospective harmonized set of principles and rules regulating the naming of organisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Code of Phytosociological Nomenclature (Plant Associations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 1976 the International Society for Vegetation Science published a formal code of nomenclature for communities of plant species (International Code of Phytosociological Nomenclature). The third edition of the code was jointly prepared by the IAVS and FIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides references to editions (1976, 1986, 2000) and identifies this code as governing names for plant community (association) taxonomy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved Lists of Bacterial Names
rubrics_metrics.description: The Approved Lists of Bacterial Names consist of two Lists published on 1 January 1980 in the IJSB: Approved List 1 (Names of taxa above the rank of genus) and Approved List 2 (Names of genera, species, and subspecies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes Corrigenda (1984) and reprints (1989). States that names validly published since 1 January 1980 are included in subsequent publications (Moore et al. 1985; Moore and Moore 1989) and provides bibliographic pointers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published sources for names of prokaryotic, algal, protozoal, fungal, and viral taxa (Appendix 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 3 lists the major publications and resources that are sources for names across groups (Prokaryotes, Cyanobacteria, Algae, Protozoa, Fungi, Viruses, General).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For prokaryotes: 'Due to the introduction of the Approved Lists of Bacterial Names in 1980, names published prior to 1980 that did not appear on either of the Approved Lists or the Corrigenda to the Approved Lists no longer have standing in nomenclature.' 'Prokaryotic names validly published since 1980 can be found in the IJSEM as articles, Notification Lists and Validation Lists.' Points to Taxonomic Outline of Bacteria and Archaea and various indexes/databases (Index Bergeyana, AlgaeBase, MycoBank, ICTV, Catalogue of Life) as practical sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserved and Rejected Names of Prokaryotic Taxa (Appendix 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix 4 enumerates lists of conserved and rejected names of prokaryotic taxa (LIST 1: Conserved and rejected family names; LIST 2: Conserved names of genera of prokaryotes; LIST 3: Conserved specific epithets; LIST 4: Rejected names of genera and subgenera; LIST 5: Rejected specific and subspecific epithets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that citations are to the International Bulletin of Bacteriological Nomenclature and Taxonomy up to vol. 15 (1965), then to IJSB/IJSEM volumes thereafter; provides example formatting of conserved/rejected entries and notes 'Opinion no.' and citation pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural guidance for virus nomenclature changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Ratified changes to the International Code of Nomenclature of Viruses will be published in Virology Division News in Archives of Virology, and in subsequent ICTV Reports. Also refer to the Minutes of the Meetings of the International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses for actions on proposals to change the code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the official publication channels and minutes to consult for authoritative, ratified changes to virus nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of cyanobacteria under competing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyanobacteria continue to be covered by both the Botanical Code and Prokaryotic Code. An effort to reconcile the status of this group of bacteria has been underway for several decades, though a final decision has not yet been reached between the ICN and ICSP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References specific proposal and literature (Oren, 2004) proposing further integration of cyanobacteria under the Bacteriological Code; flags this as an ongoing area of reconciliation between codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: General bibliographic and index resources for nomenclature
rubrics_metrics.description: A collection of reference works and indexes serve as the authoritative sources for names and nomenclatural changes (Index Bergeyana, Index Nominum Genericorum, Approved Lists, Ainsworth & Bisby's Dictionary of the Fungi, MycoBank, AlgaeBase, ICTV taxonomy releases, Species 2000 & ITIS Catalogue of Life, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specific citations and URLs where available; notes how to use these resources to trace bibliographic history and current status of names.
